$comment: Allow-list record for the repo ROOT and docs/. No gate or CI rung checks it: ADR-0311 D2 retired `check:manifest`, and the uninvoked script was deleted when this section moved into the fragment tree (ADR-0556), so it binds the author. Adding a NEW top-level root entry, or a NEW standalone doc under docs/, REQUIRES adding it here with a justification first — that friction is the point: it blocks temp/ad-hoc junk at root and keeps durable project knowledge in the Library (definition/principle/pattern/guardrail/techstack/adr/open-question), not loose prose docs. A new doc's justification must say why it does NOT belong in the Library. See the `repo-surface-allowlist` Library guardrail.

allowedDirs.design: Owner-approved executable HTML mocks and binary visual witnesses referenced by an arc or ADR. Their behavioural rules stay in the Library/decision record; renderable assets do not fit the Library's atomic text schema and must remain directly reviewable by humans and visual-build agents.
allowedDirs.friction-inbox: Offline/remote capture staging for `friction` Library items (ADR-0168 D2): a remote 443-only session that cannot reach the live store files `storytree friction new` here as validated doc JSON for its PR, and the adjudicator/librarian files it live and deletes the staging file (migrate-only, like sync-corpus). Schema-validated fail-closed by friction-inbox.test.ts in `pnpm -r test`. NOT durable knowledge — a transient staging surface, so it sits in docs/ rather than the Library.
allowedDirs.research: Long-form decision-provenance behind specific ADRs (option surveys / how a decision was reached). Does not fit the Library's atomic-unit model.

files.open-questions.md: The deferred-decisions backlog, cited by stable section number (§n) from the ADRs and Library units' references. A threaded cross-reference ledger, not atomic Library units.

dirs..codex: Codex project config; generated native subagents mirror the Library agent tier.
dirs..cursor: Cursor project config; generated native subagents mirror the Library agent tier (ADR-0178).
dirs..gemini: Gemini CLI project config; generated native subagents mirror the Library agent tier.
dirs..github: CI workflows (the green gate + auto-merge, ADR-0022).
dirs.docs: ADRs + open-questions backlog + research notes (see `docs` beside `root` in this file).
dirs.infra: Terraform / GCP infra (Cloud SQL, WIF/CI + studio identities, deploy pipelines). The instance runs 24/7 per ADR-0302 D2 — no scheduled stop/start.
dirs.legacy: Read-only storytree 0.1 Rust submodule (legacy/Agentic); reference only.
dirs.packages: Workspace packages (proof-protocol / storage-protocol / library / notice-board / studio-members / agent / orchestrator / drive / cli / uat-criterion; @storytree/core dissolved per ADR-0068, @storytree/store dissolved per ADR-0077; the two root ports renamed for role-not-position per ADR-0078: verdict-contract→proof-protocol, base→storage-protocol; drive carved the build/orchestrate drivers out of cli so the studio drives builds without depending on cli; uat-criterion is the per-criterion detail organism for ADR-0209 D5/D6, live-canonical since ADR-0307 D5, and since 2026-08-31 also the home of the criterion PARSER; the whole model-UAT family — model-judged-uat, model-uat-pilot and finally model-uat itself — was DELETED across ADR-0247 D5's three retirements, which withdrew ADR-0209's rubric-judge, pilot and judge-registry machinery; the one live thing model-uat still held was criterion.ts, lifted into uat-criterion rather than deleted; a model DRIVING a UAT journey is untouched and lives in @storytree/drive); art-authoring is the author-time, vendor-swappable generative-3D blocking-substrate adapter for ADR-0225 — a second art-factory-owned package that depends on procedural-architecture, NOT foundational because it carries node/network deps; forest-layout is the same shape one story over — a second forest-world-owned package holding WHERE THE ISLANDS SIT, extracted from apps/studio/src/components/TreeView.tsx on 2026-09-07 by ADR-0537 D1 and NOT foundational because it depends on forest-world. ADR-0537 ruled AGAINST folding it into forest-world itself: that package earns its keep by depending on nothing, while layout has different consumers and a far higher change rate, and only forest-world/src and forest-world-r3f/src are mirrored to the website, so a package outside them pays no publishing toll — which is the toll that had kept the packing surface-side).
dirs.repo-manifest: The manifest's authoritative fragments (ADR-0556) and its only authoring surface: one directory per domain (repo-surface, package-ownership, source-ownership with one file per owner, hierarchy-camps, hosted-stories), composed by packages/drive/src/manifest-fragments.ts. No composed aggregate is committed beside it (repo-manifest-aggregate-leaves-git), and `pnpm check:manifest-fragments` holds every fragment to the one form the composer writes.
dirs.scripts: Repo-level maintenance scripts (e.g. the gate's background launcher and the session hooks).
dirs.stories: The story-tree seed: the work-hierarchy corpus, schema-validated by packages/library.

files..env.example: Sample env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); DB auth is keyless.
files..gcloudignore: Upload filter for `gcloud builds submit` (the hosted studio image, ADR-0042); must sit at the upload root, which is the repo root.
files.AGENTS.md: Generated Codex root/session guidance from the canonical Library session-orchestrator agent (ADR-0291).
files.README.md: Project front-door (the one standalone narrative doc we keep).
files.tsconfig.base.json: Shared TS compiler options every package extends.
files.web: storytree-web (the public front-door site) vendored as a submodule; wired in .gitmodules (PR #111).
